terra.problem: The comparison suggests Jephthah checked in before moving out. The text says the Spirit came upon him; it does not describe him checking in.
The statement that angels appear elsewhere in the Bible is an outside Bible fact without a reference.
The joke does not make clear why a sleeping Jephthah would wake to a quiet army. The image does not click on its own.
It states that his daughter came out to celebrate his return. The text says she came out to meet him with tambourines and dancing, but does not state that reason.
The text does not say his daughter was the first one through the door.
Saying his daughter was leading the dancing adds a detail the text does not give.
The reference to the elders being in the larger story is an outside-passage Bible fact without its own reference.
Saying the text does not put an army in the room suggests Jephthah made the vow in a room. The text does not give its location.
Being Jephthah's only child does not establish that his daughter had no sisters through her mother.
He grants her request, but the text does not say he does so right away.
The text says she mourned, but does not say the time in the mountains was quiet.
